resources.string: StandBy clock is on. Tap to close.
StandBy Clock turns your Android phone into a bedside display while charging.
Place it horizontally on a stand.
For StandBy to appear on its own after you lock the phone, either keep StandBy open (tap Start StandBy, then lock) or set StandBy Clock as your screen saver below.
Automatic StandBy on the lock screen

Android lets apps appear on a locked phone automatically only through the system screen saver. Choose “StandBy Clock” as the screen saver and set it to start while charging. When the screen times out on the charger, StandBy appears over the lock screen; in landscape you get the full display, otherwise it turns the screen off after 30 seconds.

StandBy can be shown on top of the lock screen but never unlocks your phone or replaces your secure lock screen. Notifications and apps stay protected. Exiting StandBy while locked returns you to your normal lock screen.

Samsung: the screen saver is under Settings › Display › Screen saver (some One UI versions hide it; search Settings for “Screen saver”). Disable “Put app to sleep” for StandBy Clock in Battery settings if StandBy closes unexpectedly.

OnePlus: if Settings › Display (or Settings search: “screen saver”) offers a screen saver, choose StandBy Clock with “While charging”. Without a charger, use the NiteStand Quick Settings tile, or turn on “Lock-screen auto start” and set App info › Battery usage to “Unrestricted” so OxygenOS does not stop it. Open Diagnostics to see what your phone allows.

Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: HyperOS and MIUI usually remove the system screen saver. Use Start StandBy, then lock the phone. Set Battery saver to “No restrictions” for StandBy Clock and enable “Show on Lock screen” in the app\'s Other permissions.
OPPO / realme: ColorOS may hide the screen saver. Use Start StandBy, then lock. Allow “Show on lock screen” / floating windows for StandBy Clock if the lock screen hides it.
vivo / iQOO: Funtouch / OriginOS may hide the screen saver. Use Start StandBy, then lock. Allow “Lock screen display” for StandBy Clock in app permissions if needed.
Pixel: Settings › Display › Screen saver › StandBy Clock, then “When to start” › While charging. Pixel tablets also offer Hub mode, which is a separate system feature.
Motorola: Settings › Display › Screen saver (if present) supports StandBy Clock. Otherwise use Start StandBy and lock the phone.
If your phone has Settings › Display › Screen saver, choose StandBy Clock there for fully automatic StandBy. Otherwise use Start StandBy and then lock the phone.

Android only starts screen savers while charging or docked, and apps cannot open themselves from the background. Without a charger, start StandBy with one tap from the NiteStand tile in Quick Settings (also works on the lock screen), or turn on “Lock-screen auto start” in Settings so StandBy opens when you wake the locked phone while it is horizontal.
